extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants and attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive requirements for claiming and examining foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. §119(a)-(d)/(f), including submission, timeliness, identification, translations, file-entry, and remedies to perfect priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy requirement for right of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) and (f) requires that a copy of the original foreign application, specification, and drawings certified by the patent office of the foreign country in which filed, shall be submitted to the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office, in order for an applicant to be entitled to the right of priority in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 4A(2) of the Paris Convention recognizes equivalent filings, but the statute requires a certified copy; AIPA (Nov. 29, 2000) amended 35 U.S.C.119(b)(3) to require certification by the foreign intellectual property authority in which the foreign application was filed for applications filed under 35 U.S.C.111(a) and international applications complying with 35 U.S.C.371 with filing dates on or after Nov. 29, 2000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable evidence for German design deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the prior 'regular national filing' consisted of the deposit of an actual model (e.g., German 'Geschmacksmuster' deposited at an Amtsgericht), the USPTO will receive drawings or acceptable clear photographs of the deposited model faithfully reproducing the design together with other required information, certified as being a true copy by an official of the court with which the model was originally deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Article 4D(3) of the Paris Convention allows certification 'by the authority which received such application', certification by the German court is sufficient; additional certification by the German Patent Office is not necessary. Authentication is not required under Article 4D(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification by the authority that received the application suffices
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference to 'patent office' in 35 U.S.C.119 is construed to extend to the authority in charge of the design register (e.g., appropriate court), so certification by that receiving authority satisfies the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interpretation aligns with the Paris Convention's Article 4D(3) and removes need for extra certification from the foreign patent office in jurisdictions where filings are handled by another authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate disclosure under 35 U.S.C.112 required for priority
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign application must contain a disclosure of the invention adequate to satisfy the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112 in order to form the basis for the right of priority in a later filed United States application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of a certified copy alone may not perfect priority if the foreign filing lacks sufficient disclosure; examiners must assess sufficiency of disclosure when determining entitlement to the foreign filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim identification and contents required by statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C.119(b)(1), a claim for priority must identify the foreign application by specifying the application number, the intellectual property authority or country in which the application was filed, and the date of filing the application at such time during the pendency of the application as required by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require certified copies, translations, and other information; failure to present the claim in the required form may be treated as a waiver under 119(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of foreign priority claim (37 CFR 1.55 deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: For original applications filed under 35 U.S.C.111(a) (other than design) on or after Nov. 29, 2000, the claim for priority must be presented during pendency and within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application (see 37 CFR 1.55(a)(1)(i)); analogous PCT time limits apply to national stage entries (37 CFR 1.55(a)(1)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any claim not presented within the time period in 37 CFR 1.55(a)(1) is considered waived, unless accompanied by a grantable petition to accept an unintentionally delayed claim under 37 CFR 1.55(c). Examiners should notify applicants of untimely claims (e.g., form paragraph 2.21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when priority claim is untimely
rubrics_metrics.description: If the foreign priority claim is submitted after the time period set in 37 CFR 1.55(a)(1)(i) and without a petition under 37 CFR 1.55(c), the examiner may notify applicant that the foreign priority claim will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 2.21. If a petition under 1.55(c) is filed and grantable (showing unintentional delay), the claim may be accepted with surcharge per 37 CFR 1.17(t).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of timely and regular papers into application file history
rubrics_metrics.description: When the papers under 35 U.S.C.119(a)-(d) are received within the time period set in 37 CFR 1.55(a)(1) and are regular in form with no irregularities in dates, they are entered into the application file history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner will acknowledge receipt using form PTOL-326 or form paragraph 2.26; for Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing see the IFW Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistency between certified copy and oath/declaration or ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: If the certified copy filed does not correspond to the foreign application identified in the oath/declaration or application data sheet (ADS), or if the oath/declaration/ADS does not refer to the particular foreign application, the applicant has not complied with 37 CFR 1.63.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should require applicant to explain the inconsistency and to file a new oath/declaration or ADS stating correctly the facts concerning foreign applications required by 37 CFR 1.63, using form paragraph 2.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment when certified copy filed but no claim made
rubrics_metrics.description: If a certified copy has been filed in a parent application but no claim for priority is present in the child application, the examiner should acknowledge the filing of the certified copy and note that a claim for priority must be filed to obtain benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 2.22 to acknowledge presence of certified copy in parent application and to enter specified information in MPEP §202.03 on the file wrapper or PALM bib-data sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign filing more than 12 months before U.S. filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim for priority under 35 U.S.C.119(a)-(d) cannot be based on an earlier foreign application if that application was filed more than 12 months prior to the U.S. application filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 2.23 to notify applicant. However, where a provisional filing and a later complete foreign filing exist (e.g., British provisional vs complete), entitlement may be based on the complete specification if within one year; note how printed heading will reflect claimed priority for subject matter not disclosed in provisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: When certified copy is not of the earliest foreign filing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the certified copy filed is not the first foreign application for which priority is claimed, the examiner should notify applicant that the date claimed is not the date of the first-filed foreign application acknowledged in the oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 2.24 to inform the applicant that the claimed foreign priority date is not the earliest foreign filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: No certified copy filed despite claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Where priority is claimed but no certified copy of the foreign application has been filed, applicant has not complied with 35 U.S.C.119(b) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 2.25 to require that applicant file the certified copy and provide application-specific details in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning foreign priority papers
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be necessary to return papers filed under 35 U.S.C.119(a)-(d) upon applicant request (e.g., to obtain a translation) or because they fail to meet a basic statutory requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the papers have not been entered into the application file history, return does not require Director approval but should be sent to the Technology Center (TC) Director for cancellation of Office stamps. If entered into the file history, return requires approval of the Director of the USPTO and should be forwarded to the TC Director; approval should be entered into the file history. Questions directed to the Office of the Commissioner for Patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation in file history and PALM bib-data sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: Where foreign applications are listed on the oath/declaration or ADS, the examiner should ensure they are properly listed on the PALM bib-data sheet, correcting typographical or format errors and initialing the 'verified' line when matching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an error exists on the oath/declaration or ADS, require a new oath/declaration or ADS where appropriate. If a foreign application listed on the oath/decl/ADS is not listed on the PALM bib-data sheet, provide application number, country, and filing date on the PALM bib-data sheet and forward it to the Legal Instrument Examiner for correction. Applications listed but filed in non-qualifying countries should be lined through in ink. See MPEP §201.13 for list of qualifying countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper identification and formatting of foreign application numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the provided tables to determine acceptable presentation forms of foreign application numbers and the 'Minimum Significant Part of the Number' which should be used in USPTO records to uniquely identify an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow country-specific rules: eliminate alpha symbols preceding numerals except Hungary; eliminate decimal characters except France; reduce use of dashes but retain essential elements for Czechoslovakia and Japan. The tables give examples and the simplified formats for many countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's treatment when encountering an intervening reference
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner finds a reference with an effective date between the foreign filing date and the U.S. filing date, the examiner rejects claims considered unpatentable over that reference unless priority papers are of record demonstrating entitlement to the foreign date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If papers are not yet filed, applicant may argue or submit papers; form paragraph 2.19 ('Overcome Rejection by Translation') may be used. If papers are filed but not in English, require an English translation with a statement of accuracy. If papers are in file and examiner determines applicant entitled to the date, withdrawal of the rejection is appropriate; otherwise repeat the rejection with reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement and accuracy statement
rubrics_metrics.description: When foreign papers are not in English and are presented for the purpose of overcoming a reference or determining entitlement to a foreign filing date, a translation into English is required together with a statement that the translation is accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When examiner requires filing of papers, translation should be required at the same time. If no translation is present, the examiner may reject unpatentable claims and require an English translation to determine entitlement to the date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity of invention and sufficiency examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The most important aspect of determining right of priority is whether the U.S. and foreign applications disclose the same invention; the foreign application may be considered as if filed in the U.S. on the foreign date, but must be examined for sufficiency of disclosure under 35 U.S.C.112 and for basis of the claims sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may be entitled to the foreign filing date for some claims but not others; entitlement may come from different foreign applications for different claim sets. Examiners must study the foreign papers to determine identity and sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of papers filed after payment of issue fee but before grant
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claim for foreign priority or the certified copy is filed after payment of the issue fee but prior to grant of the patent, the priority claim or certified copy must be accompanied by a processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The priority claim or certified copy will be placed in the file record but there will be no review and the patent when published will not include the priority claim. A certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C.255 and 37 CFR 1.323 can be filed to have the priority claim considered after publication. For original applications filed under 35 U.S.C.111(a) on or after Nov. 29, 2000, an additional grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.55(c) must be filed with the certificate of correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using certificate of correction or reissue to perfect priority
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C.255 and 37 CFR 1.323 may be requested and issued to perfect a claim for foreign priority benefit in a patented continuing application if the requirements of 35 U.S.C.119(a)-(d) or (f) had been satisfied in the parent application prior to issuance and the requirements of 37 CFR 1.55(a) are met; otherwise a reissue application may be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law (Brenner v. State of Israel; In re Van Esdonk) provide precedent for when certificate of correction or reissue can remedy failure to perfect a priority claim. If requirements were not satisfied in the patented application (or its parent) or 37 CFR 1.55(a) not met, perfection can only be by reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special handling for provisional or incomplete foreign specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain foreign provisional specifications (e.g., UK provisional specification) may not contain a complete disclosure as required by 35 U.S.C.112; reliance on a provisional may be insufficient and entitlement may instead rely on a later complete specification if presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must assess completeness of disclosure in provisional filings; if insufficient, rely on the complete specification's date if presented (treated as a different application) and adjust priority accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph usage and examiner notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific form paragraphs (e.g., 2.19, 2.21, 2.22, 2.23, 2.24, 2.25, 2.26, 2.27) are prescribed for acknowledging papers, notifying applicants of defects, and explaining examiner actions regarding foreign priority papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate form paragraph based on the situation: untimely claims, inconsistent or missing oath/declaration references, certified copies filed but no claim, foreign filing more than 12 months earlier, claimed date not earliest, no certified copy filed, acknowledgement of papers placed in record, and acknowledgment in parent application, respectively.
